name: Jio Financial Services Ltd
about: JFSL was originally incorporated as Reliance Strategic Investments Private Limited in July, 1999 under the Companies Act 1956.  Jio Financial Services Limited was incorporated in  July, 23. JFSL is a NBFC-ND-SI registered with RBI. The company is a holding company and will operate its financial services business through its consumer-facing subsidiaries namely Jio Finance Limited (JFL), Jio Insurance Broking Limited (JIBL), and Jio Payment Solutions Limited (JPSL) and joint venture namely Jio Payments Bank Limited (JPBL). [1]

sections.one_liner: Reliance-linked financial holding company: Jio Credit lending is booming, but ROE is 1.2% and core group profit isn't growing yet.
business: Core Investment Company, RBI-registered: Borrow (Jio Credit NBFC), Transact (payments), Protect (insurance), Invest (JioBlackRock), with 23M app users. [AR FY26]
FY26 revenue of ₹3,543cr: 54% interest, 17% fees/commissions, 21% treasury gains, 8% dividends. Nearly a third is market or dividend driven. [AR FY26]
Lending is the only business at scale: ₹25,711cr AUM against ₹544cr payments-bank deposits and ₹15,200cr AMC AUM at FY26. [AR FY26] [Q4FY26 call]
Loan book mix: 45% mortgages, 44% corporate/SME, 10% loans against securities. Unsecured consumer exposure is not disclosed. [Q1FY27 call]
financial_snapshot: Q2 FY27: revenue ₹1,699cr (+73% YoY, -15% QoQ), PAT ₹340cr (-51% YoY), OPM 63% vs 70% a year ago. [Numbers]
TTM: revenue ₹5,623cr, EBITDA ₹3,635cr (65% margin), PAT ₹1,711cr. PAT/revenue is 30%, swinging between 20% and 41% by quarter. [Numbers]
Valuation: market cap ₹1,35,034cr, P/E 78.9, P/B 1.04x (₹204 vs ₹196 book), at the 52-week low of ₹203. [Numbers]
Returns are tiny: ROE 1.19%, ROCE 1.86%, dividend yield 0.29%. About ₹1.3 lakh crore of equity earns about ₹1,700cr a year. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue grew at a 38% CAGR over FY24–26 (₹1,855cr to ₹3,521cr). The 328% 3-year CAGR comes off a ₹45cr FY23 base and isn't meaningful. [Numbers]
PAT is flat: ₹1,605cr, ₹1,613cr, then ₹1,561cr (-1.4% CAGR). Revenue growth is not reaching group earnings. [Numbers]
OPM fell from 84% (FY24) to 66% (FY26). Funding and operating costs are replacing near-costless treasury income. [Numbers]
Jio Credit compounds: AUM ₹19,049cr (Q3 FY26) to ₹37,320cr (Q2 FY27); quarterly disbursements rose from ₹8,615cr to ₹13,135cr. [Q2FY27 call]
balance_sheet: Borrowings went from ₹0 (FY24) to ₹21,768cr (Mar 26) to ₹41,325cr (Sep 26), up 90% in six months. [Numbers]
H1 FY27 borrowings rose ₹19,557cr while AUM rose about ₹11,600cr, so debt is running ahead of the loan book. Why isn't disclosed. [Numbers] [Q2FY27 call]
Consolidated D/E is 0.32, but Jio Credit is above 3x (CAR 25.91%). Net worth fell ₹4,258cr in H1 despite ₹1,170cr PAT; the cause isn't disclosed. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]
cash_quality: FY24–26 cumulative CFO is -₹26,206cr against ₹4,779cr PAT, so CFO/PAT is -5.48. [Numbers]
FCF equals CFO each year (capex not disclosed). Outflow widened from ₹678cr to ₹15,439cr, roughly tracking loan-book growth. [Numbers]
For a lender, negative CFO comes from growth; the real test is credit cost. GNPA and credit costs are not disclosed in any call. [Q2FY27 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: The call says Q2 total income grew 132% YoY; NUMBERS show revenue +73% (₹1,699cr vs ₹981cr). Definitions differ, and neither reconciliation is disclosed. [Q2FY27 call] [Numbers]
Q1 PAT of ₹830cr (+156%) was dividend-led: excluding dividends, PBT rose only 18% to ₹461cr. Q2 PAT then fell 51% YoY. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
The 'zero tech-debt cost leverage' claim conflicts with OPM falling from 84% to 66% over two years and to 63% in Q2. [Q2FY27 call] [Numbers]
The call highlights payments growth, but JPSL TPV fell 24% QoQ (₹19,208cr to ₹14,682cr) without comment; margin rose to 14bps. [Q1FY27 call] [Q2FY27 call]
guidance: Bank of America to invest about ₹18,000cr in Jio Credit, about ₹9,500cr upfront, subject to approvals; about 14% of group net worth. [Q2FY27 call]
BlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund (GIFT City) is due to launch in Q3 FY27. [Q2FY27 call]
Securities broking beta launch was promised for Q2 FY27. Separately, a 'Personal CFO' or JioScore is due in the 'near future'. [Q1FY27 call]
Jio Credit plans to enter new credit segments and widen touchpoints over the medium term. No numeric AUM, margin or ROE targets have been given. [Q4FY26 call]
Jio Allianz general insurance approvals are 'progressing satisfactorily'. Life insurance is still on a non-binding agreement. No dated horizon. [Q1FY27 call]

bull: Jio Credit Q2: AUM +154%, NII +116% to ₹302cr, PAT +140% to ₹120cr, record ₹13,135cr disbursements. [Q2FY27 call]
The stock trades at 1.04x book and its 52-week low, while BoA's ₹18,000cr validates the lending arm's value. [Numbers] [Q2FY27 call]
Fee businesses are improving: JioBlackRock AUM +24% QoQ to ₹22,746cr; payments margin up from 9 to 14bps; 3.2cr app users. [Q2FY27 call]
bear: P/E of 78.9 on 1.19% ROE. Group PAT has been flat for three years, and Jio Credit's ₹120cr is only 35% of Q2 PAT. [Numbers] [Q2FY27 call]
Leverage is building fast: borrowings up 10x in 18 months to ₹41,325cr, CFO -₹15,439cr, and asset quality is not disclosed. [Numbers]
Earnings depend on treasury and dividends (29% of revenue). PAT swings from ₹269cr to ₹830cr; the AR also flags material related-party transactions. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
questions: What are Jio Credit's GNPA, credit cost and ROE at ₹37,320cr AUM?
Why did borrowings rise ₹19,557cr in H1 while AUM grew only ₹11,600cr?
What drove the ₹4,258cr H1 net worth decline despite ₹1,170cr profit?
Why did JPSL TPV fall 24% QoQ, and did securities broking launch?

annual_report.business: Jio Financial Services Limited (JFSL) is a Core Investment Company registered with RBI, operating as a holding company providing digital financial services through subsidiaries and joint ventures across four customer needs: Borrow (lending via NBFC), Transact (payments), Protect (insurance), Invest (wealth/asset management). Reaches 23 million users via JioFinance app.

segments.name: Lending (Jio Credit NBFC)
segments.comment: Interest income driven. Home loans, LAP, securities lending, enterprise leasing. ₹25,711Cr AUM FY26.

segments.name: Fees & Commission (Payments, Insurance, Advisory)
segments.comment: Payment solutions ₹52,226Cr TPV, insurance broking 42 partners, asset/wealth management, banking fees

segments.name: Treasury & Investment Gains
segments.comment: Fair value changes on fixed income investments. FY26 impacted by geopolitical yield spike March 2026.

segments.name: Dividend Income
segments.comment: Dividends from subsidiaries and associates including Reliance entities

annual_report.revenue_mix: 100% India-focused operations across digital platforms. Consolidated revenue ₹3,543Cr: 54% interest income, 17% fees/commissions, 21% investment gains, 8% dividends. 23M unique users, 9M monthly active users on JioFinance app.
strategy: Transform JioFinance app into unified digital marketplace integrating lending, banking, insurance, wealth management
Deploy Agentic AI and neural networks for hyper-personalized product recommendations and customer segmentation
Expand via global partnerships: BlackRock (asset management, wealth, broking) and Allianz (insurance, reinsurance)
Maximize customer lifetime value through cross-selling, data-driven personalization, ecosystem integration
Scale profitably from foundational infrastructure phase to aggressive revenue growth across all verticals
annual_report.outlook: Transitioning from foundational infrastructure development into aggressive scaling. Immediate focus on sustainable revenue growth across all core verticals. BlackRock and Allianz partnerships expand asset management, wealth advisory, broking and insurance underwriting capabilities globally.
risks: Macroeconomic sensitivity: interest rate movements, inflation, geopolitical tensions (West Asia) impact NIM and credit demand
Regulatory risk: adverse law changes, new regulations or interpretation shifts affecting cost structure and operating flexibility
Cybersecurity and AI-driven fraud threats requiring continuous capital-intensive investments in advanced security frameworks
Reputational risk from negative stakeholder perception; contagion from subsidiary/JV performance affecting funding access
annual_report.flags: Material Related Party Transactions approval sought at AGM for Company and Subsidiaries (Items 6-7 in Notice). New joint statutory auditor appointment: PKF Sridhar & Santhanam LLP. Consolidated PAT declined to ₹1,561Cr from ₹1,613Cr; treasury headwinds from March 2026 yield spike offset strong NBFC growth.
